bpmStatus: DISPUTED — must be resolved by measurement before any lesson ships

bpmCandidates.note: Two research passes disagree by roughly a factor of two. R1 reported 89-100; the harvest pass found 160-180 rising to 200-220 in the instructors' own material, and even a single source (RF Dance) contradicts itself across two of its own articles. The likely cause is that the two passes measured different quantities: salsa's quick-quick-slow places three steps across four musical beats, so a 'step feel' rate and a musical beat rate differ by about 2x.
bpmCandidates.whyItMatters: The beat grid must run at the rate the dancer actually steps to. Getting it wrong by 2x does not produce slightly-off timing — it produces a grid that lines up with every other beat, so half the learner's correct steps are scored as misses and the product blames them for its own error.
bpmCandidates.resolution: G1: take one known track, tap-annotate it with tools/beat_annotate.py, and compare the fitted BPM against both candidate ranges. One measurement settles it; no further research round is warranted.

copyright.basis: Social dance; core shines such as Suzy Q trace to the 1930s and are public domain. Shines are by definition the solo, partnerless subset of the dance — the product's constraint matches the form rather than fighting it.
copyright.boundary: Named instructor routines are not reproduced; combos are our own arrangement of public step vocabulary.

honesty.$comment: K10 (plan §22) in machine-readable form: what this style grades, what it deliberately shows without grading, and WHY — every line traceable to a measurement, not a policy preference. Shown to the user; the app must not grade anything absent from `measured`.
measured: Leg shape through the step cycle — 8 leg joints (hips, knees, thighs, shins) agreed to within 1.57-5.76deg across 3 independent instructors, scored at 100% of the cycle (content/references/ss_shine_footwork.json)
Which foot leads — established by comparing your whole leg pattern against the reference both ways round, with a 15.6deg margin against a 6deg noise floor (M-F-117)
notMeasured: Arm carriage and styling — MEASURED and deliberately not graded: instructors disagree by 11-58deg on arm joints in the same footwork, so there is no single correct arm to grade you against. Shown and taught, never scored (M-F-102).

Timing against the music — the beat grid for this style is unresolved (bpmStatus DISPUTED, two research passes 2x apart). Grading timing on a grid that could be doubled would blame you for our error, so no timing judgement runs until one tap measurement settles it.

Whether you truly transferred your weight — the knee-angle change this would need to detect (1.07-3.42deg across the reference's own instructors) sits inside the pipeline's own 6deg landmark-noise floor, so a verdict would be indistinguishable from tracking jitter (M-F-117).

lessons._whyUnlocked: Only step in this style with a built reference AND a proven consumer: content/references/ss_shine_footwork.json (3 attested instructors, mirrorConfident:true) is read end-to-end by tools/ss_shine_footwork_liveness.py, which shows both live errors firing on controlled corruptions and staying silent on real footage. Family's second full chain (M-F-119).

lockedReason.en: We haven't found enough teachers for this step yet. We looked: the five salsa clips we already have were measured against what makes the basic the basic — the held count and the travelling step — and none of them contain it. Grading you against one teacher's version would just be that teacher's preference wearing a score, so this lesson stays shut until at least three independent instructors have been measured.

lessons.blockedBy: reference.collectedTakes == 0 — existing pool PROBED and named-rejected 2026-07-30 (steps/ss_basic.json reference.harvestProbe: 0/4 sources, negative control passed, method limit named)
lessons.probeNote: The rejection is measured, not assumed: tools/probe_basic_candidates.py. Bound conclusion — 'not in the windows this pipeline surfaces', not 'not in this footage' (the isolator yields ~1 window per clip and cannot split a 5-step compilation).

demoOnlyReason.en: There is no single correct arm position here — we measured it: the teachers we studied differ from each other by 11 to 58 degrees on the arms while doing the same footwork. That is style, not error. So we show you the range and let you choose; grading it would be inventing a right answer that does not exist.

lessons.evidence: content/references/ss_shine_footwork.json scoring[] — arm joints verdict coached_only / scored_partial (0-64% coverage, 11-58deg medianDispersion) while every leg joint is scored at 100%

demoOnlyReason.en: Hearing where the music's 1 falls is the heart of salsa, and a camera cannot see whether you heard it. We teach it and leave the judging to your own ears.

referencedGenericContent.note: Harvested to chase ss_suzy_q; only 1 of the 4 sources is individually named Suzy Q, the other 3 are generic shine/footwork tutorials. Legs-only pairwise distance across all 4 (4.1-7.1 deg, best orientation) is the same order as a single reference's own instructor-to-instructor dispersion — MEASURED same-movement, not eyeballed (M-F-102 reversed an earlier visual impression that they looked different). So the id names the measured generic content, not the Suzy Q figure specifically; the Suzy Q source is tagged at source level (content/references/ss_shine_footwork.json sources[].namedVariant) rather than dropped or split out. ss_suzy_q above stays reserved and unbuilt until sourced cleanly.
